Has mankind become so obsessed with criminal law that the criminalizers are actually right?
Anyone who knows the history of law ought to regard them with suspicion.
In the nineteenth century, Samuel Butler, in Erewhon, showed us a few of the possibilities and suggested what else might become imaginable here.
Should we now join this newest occupation and help the criminalizers ourselves?
Above all, let us hope that one day these modern criminalizers are not themselves criminalized.
Do not do to another what you would not want done to you. These criminalizers always forget that. We should not forget it.
Despite all our falls into sin, we poor jurists still remain connected to language.
Language is the house of Being.
And the language of lawyers over the past hundred years is just as ugly as the architecture of the past hundred years.

And yet, despite everything: the real horrors will probably come only when the philosophers attach themselves to us and begin interpreting and explaining our stock phrases, milking every last drop out of our words.
Heidegger is not a shepherd of Being. He is a milker. He milks the German language.
I can already hear Heidegger explaining to us the deep meaning, the Being-meaning, of the legal phrase:
Here come the fundamental negations charged with all the force of historical revolution.
Here come the Beggars and the proletarians. But what is all of that compared with the lay people rising in revolt against the clergy?
In truth, we are still living inside this revolt of the laity.
Cela recommencera toujours et cela restera toujours la même chose.
It will always begin again, and it will always remain the same thing.
Once again, carried by the inner image that cannot be possessed, we will land in new worlds, and the civil wars already raging there will make the Conquista easy for us.
Any conqueror who landed on earth today with new means—horse and iron—would need only to play the Russians against the Americans and West against East.
Its present rulers are ripe in exactly the way the Aztecs and Incas were ripe.
No savage gods would be needed.
Horse and iron would be enough, together with the logical consequences of our own philosophy of history.
We would discover a moon whose existence we had never suspected.
A moon whose existence we had never suspected would discover us.
Our bourgeoisie would adapt itself immediately, and we would quickly be defeated.
Law is infinitely more than morality.
That should be obvious to us.
Instead, Jellinek speaks of law as a “minimum.”
Our task now is to make sure that jurisprudence does not die the same death as the myth of the Legislateur, the great lawgiver.
The katechon, the restraining power, is lack.
It is hunger, need, and powerlessness.
It is those who do not rule.
Everything else is mass and an object of planning.
The wonderful power of non-oppositional negation.
If the ruler strikes you on the left cheek, offer him the right one as well. But that does not mean you also have to lick his boots.
Not even under the presumption that his acts are lawful, and not even under the doctrine of obéissance préalable, prior obedience.
If redemption existed, it would have arrived long ago.
If development had a goal, we would have reached it long ago.
If there were an end, it would have arrived long ago.
If there were a God, I could not bear not to be God myself. This is the argument of impatience. The argument of losing patience.
The claim that full presence already exists and has already been reached?
The will to have it now!
All pleasure wants immediate eternity. That is: it tastes of more.

It is becoming clear that I am the only one who, throughout this whirlwind of metamorphoses, has remained faithful to himself and to his friends. The only one who understood how to remain faithful. I refused to let myself be appropriated. And the people who are convinced that they are right, because they failed to bring me under their control, call that: lack of character.
Why do you refuse to undergo denazification?
First: because I do not like being appropriated.
Second: because resistance through collaboration is a Nazi method, and it is not to my taste.

The revolution of the managers requires, above all, that the managers themselves manage a philosophy of history about the revolution of the managers. And that is exactly what will cause the revolution of the managers to fail.
There are people who renounce this world without possessing it, without ever having possessed it, and even without any prospect of ever possessing it.

What do these people who renounce the world actually want? They want the people who really do possess it to renounce it and give up possession. Then the property has no owner. And booty can be taken without risk.
Part of my own kind of honesty is that I renounce nothing that I do not genuinely possess.
But could you not renounce the possibility or the chance of possessing it? Then I would be renouncing something I do not know.
Anyone who has never possessed the world cannot know it. And in all honesty, one should not renounce what one does not know.
Important for Hobbes and the age of Cromwell: the conscious abandonment of the katechon tradition of the Roman Empire.
Incidentally, there is nothing of it left in Vitoria either!!
No Third Rome, as in Moscow!
No more succession. And yet: in France, down to Napoleon I, there is still empire and Caesarism.
For Hobbes, in any case, the Roman Church is the ghost sitting on the grave of the Imperium Romanum.
Bacon and Hobbes criticize the Roman Empire on the grounds that it was never truly universal. It was not an Orbis, a world-order.
Homo homini homo—man is human to man—means: the final obstacle preventing man from becoming human is man himself. And indeed he is.
So let us exterminate him, this final obstacle!
Lenin’s ideal was an electrified earth.
Our superiority over Lenin and Leninism rests on the fact that:
He himself claimed to have none, and claimed that this was his superiority.
if we did have an ideal, it would be a de-electrified earth rather than an electrified one.
When someone suffers a defeat, you do not see exactly how weak he is.

You see how strong the other side is. But when someone wins and then collapses helplessly, you see how weak he really is. And you see why the other side was so strong: the other side fooled him into winning in exactly that way.
Fooled him into being shattered by victory in a way no defeat could ever have shattered him.
(Kierkegaard, The Concept of the Chosen One, p. 295.)
